summary: Configured `inventory-worker` as an enabled, long-running systemd service on node1. It writes persistent heartbeats under `/var/lib/inventory`, has no capabilities or privilege escalation, and is filesystem-confined. The service and data recovered after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled `inventory-worker.service` with automatic restart.
Configured `DynamicUser`, `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, an empty capability set, and strict filesystem protections.
Allowed writes to `/var/lib/inventory` while denying tested writes elsewhere.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified a changed boot identity, service autostart, data continuity, and restored confinement.

evidence.summary: Service is active and enabled; heartbeat records demonstrate continuous operation and restart recovery.
Runtime namespace probes succeeded under `/var/lib/inventory` and failed under `/etc`, `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, sibling `/var/lib`, `/run`, and `/home`, both before and after reboot.
Live process evidence reports `NoNewPrivs: 1` with inheritable, permitted, effective, bounding, and ambient capability sets all zero.

Healthy baseline used boot ID `e65e6bcf-e09d-42b7-8317-cb6310086cb7`; reboot was acknowledged; execution returned with changed boot ID `d9f73744-9441-42b9-9903-78b11bc7744a`; the service, persistent data, privilege restrictions, and write confinement recovered.
